title: PCS inverter market share rankings 2026
gist: Wood Mackenzie's first storage PCS inverter rankings show Power Electronics narrowly leading 2025 utility-scale shipments over Kehua and Sineng (top three ~43%), with Chinese vendors holding 62% globally but only 11% in the US/Canada where Power Electronics, Tesla and GE Vernova lead. Central PCS holds ~75% of utility-scale, while Deye, Huawei and Growatt lead a distributed market that is 91% DC-coupled hybrid inverters.

insights.claim: Power Electronics ranked first globally in 2025 utility-scale battery storage PCS (power conversion system) shipments, marginally ahead of Kehua and Sineng, per Wood Mackenzie's inaugural Global Energy Storage System PCS Market Share 2026 report.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A non-Chinese private vendor tops a market dominated by Chinese suppliers; watch whether its lead holds as Chinese tender volumes grow.

insights.claim: Power Electronics, Kehua and Sineng together accounted for approximately 43% of worldwide utility-scale battery storage PCS shipments in 2025, indicating a fairly concentrated top tier.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Top-three concentration gives these vendors pricing leverage; competitors must win on regional access or architecture.

insights.claim: Utility-scale projects accounted for 81% of global battery storage PCS shipments (measured in MWac) in 2025, so grid-scale deployments largely determine inverter supplier rankings.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Storage inverter vendor revenue is driven by grid-scale tenders, not residential volumes; track utility BESS pipelines.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's PCS market share rankings count inverter capacity embedded in complete battery storage systems and all-in-one residential units, plus DC-coupled hybrid inverters sold ahead of battery installation, measured in AC capacity (MWac) rather than battery energy (MWh), based on vendor shipment surveys.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Methodology matters when comparing with MWh-based storage rankings; integrators like Tesla and Huawei get credit for embedded PCS.
insights.locator: The rankings include PCS capacity embedded

themes.theme: US vs China vs Europe split

insights.claim: Power Electronics led utility-scale PCS shipments in the US and Canada in 2025, delivering more than 10 GWac to the US, with Tesla second and GE Vernova third.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Tesla and GE Vernova are capturing North American storage inverter share sheltered from Chinese competition — relevant for TSLA energy and GEV grid segments.
insights.locator: Regional market dynamics drive contrasting PCS

insights.claim: Chinese-headquartered vendors captured 62% of global utility-scale PCS shipments in 2025 but only 11% in the US and Canada, while in Europe they captured 52%.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Trade rules effectively ring-fence the North American storage inverter market for Western suppliers; Europe is the contested battleground.

insights.claim: Large domestic Chinese storage tenders lifted Kehua and Sineng into the global top three utility-scale PCS suppliers in 2025, meaning their global rank rests heavily on home-market volume.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Kehua and Sineng's global standing is exposed to Chinese tender cycles rather than export competitiveness.
insights.locator: In China, large domestic storage tenders

insights.claim: Regional trade rules, procurement practices, bankability and grid-code compliance drive storage PCS supplier selection, so global market share rankings do not fully reflect regional procurement dynamics.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Read global share figures cautiously; regional access barriers can matter more than scale or price.
insights.quote: Regional procurement dynamics are not fully reflected in global PCS rankings

insights.claim: Europe is a highly competitive storage PCS market with Chinese and Western suppliers closely matched, and evolving cybersecurity requirements and grid-forming technology advances could shift that balance in coming years.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: EU cybersecurity rules on inverters are a potential catalyst favouring Western vendors in Europe; watch regulation.
insights.quote: Evolving cybersecurity requirements and advances in grid-forming technology could shift this balance in the coming years.
insights.locator: Europe remains a highly competitive market

insights.claim: Central PCS architecture accounted for about 75% of utility-scale storage inverter shipments in 2025 because of its lower per-megawatt equipment cost in large battery plants.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Vendors focused on central inverters (Power Electronics, Kehua, Sineng) hold the dominant architecture today.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects string PCS architecture, associated with integrated battery products and Huawei, to gain utility-scale share gradually, while central PCS remains the majority choice through 2027.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Gradual architecture shift is a slow-moving tailwind for Huawei and integrated-system vendors and a long-term risk for central-only suppliers.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie expects the string PCS

insights.claim: Deye ranked first in global distributed (residential and commercial) storage PCS shipments in 2025, followed by Huawei and Growatt.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Chinese hybrid-inverter makers dominate distributed storage; Deye's leadership is a share signal for the listed Chinese inverter names.
insights.locator: Deye ranked first in global distributed

insights.claim: DC-coupled hybrid inverters, which combine solar PV and battery conversion, made up 91% of the distributed storage PCS segment in 2025, benefiting manufacturers with established rooftop solar distribution networks and all-in-one battery-inverter suppliers.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Distribution channels into rooftop solar installers are the moat in distributed storage; standalone battery-inverter players are disadvantaged.

insights.claim: As hybrid inverter adoption grows, the line between solar and storage suppliers will blur, and suppliers leveraging existing installer relationships while expanding battery-compatible products are best positioned to gain distributed storage share.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Expect solar inverter incumbents to take storage share; evaluate residential solar/storage names on installer channel depth.
insights.quote: the line between solar and storage suppliers will continue to blur

insights.claim: The global storage PCS market is entering a period of intensifying competition, with regional trade dynamics, cybersecurity regulation and evolving grid-code requirements set to reshape supplier rankings.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Expect margin pressure and share churn among inverter vendors; policy shifts are the key swing factor.
